taskDescription: Select the single-word manifestations associated with hypocalcaemic tetany.
textField: Findings under consideration include *tingling*, polyuria, *laryngospasm*, confusion, *seizures* and areflexia.

overallFeedback.feedback: Low ionised calcium lowers the neuronal firing threshold, causing spontaneous nerve discharge: tingling, laryngospasm and seizures reflect this neuromuscular excitability. Polyuria is characteristic of hypercalcaemia, while areflexia suggests hypermagnesaemia. Confusion is nonspecific and can occur with either low or high calcium.
